newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish exporters see 1996 exports below target.
newsitem.headline: Turkish exporters see 1996 exports below target.

text.p: Turkish exporters see end-1996 exports at $24.235 billion, up 7.7 percent from 1995, but slightly below an official $25 billion 1996 target, a report prepared by Turkey's biggest exporters' body said.

But hopes are high for 1997 when exports are expected to jump by 26 percent to exceed the $30 billion mark for the first time to reach $30.531 billion, the report prepared by the Turkish Exporters Assembly (TIM) said.

The report, based on data and forecasts obtained from exporter unions organised under TIM, was presented to the three-month-old Islamist-led coalition government's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on September 12.
According to the report, Turkish exporters also foresee exports to rise by 74 percent to $53.11 billion by 2000.
Exports by the locomotive readywear sector are likely to fall by three percent to $6.5 billion in 1996 when compared to 1995 figures, the report said.
But it forecasted readywear exports at $7.25 billion next year and at $11 billion in 2000.

According to the report, automotive, tobacco, electronics, wheat, cement and chemical sectors are expected increase their export figures this year by between 20 and 55 percent while drops are awaited in fruits, vegetables, olive oil, nut exports.
Exports by all sectors are expected to rise next year.

Main problems faced by the exporters were listed as the lack of a real exchange rate policy, high energy and raw material costs, insufficient Eximbank loans, delays in adjustments to be made according to European Union legislations, the report said.
Their medium and long-term expectations for government support were in the areas of marketing, development of infrastructure, energy, raw material costs, Eximbank funds and macroeconomic stability.
TIM estimated Turkish exports in the first eight months of 1996 at $14.89 billion, up 5.7 percent from the same 1995 period.
Official data put Turkey's trade deficit in January at $1.29 billion, up sharply from $547 million a year earlier.
The release of offcial trade data has been delayed by technical difficulties arising from Turkey's customs union with the European Union since January 1.
Turkey had set its 1996 targets at $25 billion for exports and $41 billion for imports after $21.6 billion and $35.7 billion, respectively last year.
